Thunderstorms offer a naturally occurring source of seismic energy that is already spread across the landscape.
Our thunderquake study revealed four distinct areas where seismic waves traveled much more slowly than through the surrounding rock.
Back on Earth, the atmosphere is constantly interacting with the ground beneath our feet.

article.title: Earth’s oceans just hit their hottest temperature ever recorded

That’s not as hot as a warm bath, but it is the hottest the world’s oceans have been since C3S started keeping records in 1979.
“As a climate scientist, this is not surprising to me all,” says Zachary Labe, a climate scientist at Climate Central, a climate research nonprofit.
The previous high, with a temperature of 21.09 degrees C (69.96 degrees F), occurred in March 2024, C3S said in a statement.
This cyclic climate pattern is marked by unusually hot Pacific Ocean temperatures, which can affect the entire planet’s weather.
